extraction.Name: Lee Ely; George King
extraction.Refused/Protested: with protest (Lee Ely); OV [unclear abbreviation, possibly 'without protest'] (George King)
extraction.Recorded patent: Yes, filed for record (Lee Ely); Not by allottee (George King)
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Mortgaged for $2000, mortgage foreclosed and redemption expired (Lee Ely); All sold (George King)
extraction.Buyer: Mortgage held by John Knox, also in settlement of old debts; John Knox is still living, and making his home in Calif. (Lee Ely); Miller Brothers of Marland, Oklahoma (George King)
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Mortgaged foreclosed and redemption expired; The price for which land was mortgaged was not the actual value of the land (Lee Ely); No money was received by allottee for this land (George King)
extraction.Occupation/Income: Income from inherited land, about $25.00 per year. No contributions from any source. (Lee Ely); Income from lease on 80 acres, $160 per annum (George King)
extraction.NOTES: Lee Ely: good health, no money accumulated; wife is dependent upon him; patent receipt: Yes; patent accepted with protest; allotment No. 206; document executed November 22, 1928; notary commission expires Aug. 3rd 1931; County of Kay, State of Oklahoma. George King: poor health; has $300.00 with income of $160.00 per annum; wife and one daughter are dependents; allotment No. 166; appears to have been defrauded by the Miller Brothers of Marland, Oklahoma — he states he did not know a patent was to be issued, believed the land was being sold by the Department, and that no money was paid him by the Miller Brothers; patent not filed for record by allottee; document executed November 20, 1928; County of Kay, State of Oklahoma; notary commission expires Aug. 3rd 1931; S 61391 file reference noted.
extraction.Literate/Illiterate: George King signed with an X mark
